text:
Project process. Every change of code and spec is an OpenSpec Change under WARRANT (schema warrant-sdd), from intent to archive in three PRs — spec, impl, archive; their steps are in the skill `slice`, file `.claude/skills/slice/change.md`, and a session follows them as written. The state of a Change is `warrant status`, the gates of a transition `warrant verify <change>`; a `warrant` error names its fix in `hint` — follow it. A session runs `warrant` commands that name a Change only on its own Change; the coordinator, and a judge of another's PR, only those that leave nothing in the repository.

Records (`.warrant/changes/**`), evidence, waivers, Runs and `openspec/specs/**` are written only by `warrant`; never edit them by hand, never call `openspec archive`. In a Change, the agent edits files of the repository only inside the `write_scope` of the active Run (what `warrant` and a git merge write are not its edits): `specify` the artifacts; `implement` narrowed with `--scope` to the source and test paths its design names plus `openspec/changes/<change>/**`. Never bypass a guard `deny` through the shell — narrow the work or ask the maintainer. A review subagent reads with the file tools and runs no shell command but `warrant run submit`; the session puts into its prompt what it needs from GitHub.

Parallel work (`design-next` SL-T08). An AREA is one spec and the prefix of its REQ/SCN ids. The AREAs of a Change are declared in `Where:` of its issue before `warrant init change`; after it an AREA is added only by a maintainer's `[decision]` naming the Change and the AREA, except `AR`, which a `skip_specs` Change (it declares none) adds itself when it needs an UNKNOWN. A Change holds its AREAs from `init` until its archive-PR is merged (or it is `ABANDONED`); one Change holds an AREA at a time, a second waits. At most three Changes are in implementation at once, from the first commit of the impl-PR until its merge. A fix of a red `main` (`fix-main-<issue>`) is exempt from the cap and from every AREA hold. One worktree and one session per Change; its three branches are made there in turn, each from fresh `origin/main`. Two parallel Changes never share a source path; files shared by several modules belong to the skeleton of the slice, and a later change of one is a separate small Change. What is held and what may start is computed by `node .claude/skills/slice/status.mjs`; after `init` a session runs it on its Change, and on a collision stops and asks on the umbrella.

Decision log. An umbrella comment whose first line starts with `[decision]` (the maintainer's, posted by the coordinator or, quoting the answer, by the session the maintainer answered), `[scope]` or `[broadcast]` binds the sessions it touches; the session acts on it, then acknowledges it by a reply on the umbrella (outside a slice: on its issue) that links it and names the Change. `[incident]` records a failure. Before `SPECIFIED` and before asking for a merge a session runs `status.mjs <change>`, reads what it lists — the entries it has not acknowledged and the comments of its own issue newer than its last push — and brings its work in line first. A slice decision that changes an open PR stops its merge: the coordinator turns the PR to draft, turns its auto-merge off and comments `⛔ Do not merge — <decision URL>`; a draft PR is never merged.

PRs. A spec-PR is offered only with `SPECIFIED` as its last commit; an impl-PR ends with `VERIFYING`, after an implementation review (skill `code-review`) stated in its body. Before a push that opens or updates a PR the owner runs `node .claude/skills/slice/judge.mjs` and pushes only when it reports no violation of the PR. The merge is a merge commit by the maintainer and is the approval; it is requested once, in the act queue (rule `maintainer-acts`), when no check has failed. A PR is owned by the session that opened it, and only the owner watches it: it binds the PR in the desktop app with auto-fix on (or tells the maintainer its CI is not watched; CI is never polled), starts `node .claude/skills/slice/wait-pr.mjs <N>` in the background right after the push that makes it wait for the maintainer, acts on its outcome, and starts its watchers again when it resumes.

Questions. A question of the spec is an UNKNOWN, decided by the maintainer's comment in the spec-PR; an implementation question, a change the spec review asks for after `SPECIFIED`, and a spec change after approval are `I-N` rows in `design.md` with the maintainer's decision.

Architecture (`design-next` ST-A01…ST-A04): at the end of every wave and on a trigger of ST-A02 the coordinator runs an architecture audit of `src/` against `design-next` into `design-next/reviews/`, grilled with the maintainer; an accepted finding that can be checked mechanically becomes a fitness test, the others a rule with an ID; a refactor is a separate Change that changes no behaviour.

The maintainer is `roles.maintainer` in `.warrant/warrant.json`. Commit and push go to your own branch; `main`, and `gh pr merge` except `--disable-auto`, are the maintainer's only.
